source.title: 서울대 한국어 플러스 3B Student’s Book & 문법 + Workbook
source.vocabulary: Entries from opening-page vocabulary boxes (standard) and bottom-of-page Korean–English notes on other pages (hard). Original glossary IDs retained. Opposites joined with a slash in the book are separate cards.
source.grammar: All 33 patterns in the grammar booklet contents. Quiz sentences and explanations are original, not textbook exercises.
source.coverage: Units10–18: student-book opening vocabulary boxes (Standard), student-book other-page notes plus workbook lesson/review footnotes (Hard), and33 indexed grammar patterns with66 original practice questions.
source.verification: Opening-page boxes and bottom vocabulary notes on printed pages 24–161 visually checked against the supplied scan. Added 그녀 and 반대하다 from page 81, which were absent from the previous glossary-based data. Cultural-page bottom notes are included in hard mode under the preceding subchapter. No running-text vocabulary added.

workbook.vocabulary: Korean–English vocabulary footnotes on printed lesson and review pages14–175; all entries are Hard. Exercise word banks are excluded.
workbook.verification: All workbook footers visually checked. Front matter, unit dividers, listening scripts and answer-key pages contain no additional vocabulary footnotes.

questions.prompt:
어제는 춥___ 오늘은 따뜻하네요.
Target grammar: -더니 — observed change or result.
questions.explanation: Yesterday was cold, but today is warm: contrast with a personally observed earlier state.

questions.prompt:
어제는 바람이 불___ 오늘은 조용해요.
Target grammar: -더니 — observed change or result.
questions.explanation: Use -더니: observed change or result.

questions.prompt:
컴퓨터가 느리면 다시 시작하___?
Target grammar: -지 그래요? — suggest doing something.
questions.explanation: Use this ending to suggest an action.

questions.prompt:
목이 아프면 따뜻한 물을 마시___?
Target grammar: -지 그래요? — suggest doing something.
questions.explanation: Use -지 그래요?: suggest doing something.

grammar.meaning: make or let someone do something

questions.prompt:
아이가 잘 볼 수 있게 의자를 ___. (높다 → causative)
Target grammar: 사동 (-이/히/리/기/우/추-) — make or let someone do something.
questions.explanation: 높이다 is the causative of 높다: raise something.

questions.prompt:
아기에게 우유를 ___. (먹다 → causative, past polite)
Target grammar: 사동 (-이/히/리/기/우/추-) — make or let someone do something.
questions.explanation: Use 사동 (-이/히/리/기/우/추-): make or let someone do something.

questions.prompt:
집에 도착하___ 열쇠가 없었어요.

questions.explanation: The realization occurs after arriving.

questions.prompt:
사진을 찍___ 뒤에 친구가 있었어요.
Target grammar: -고 보니 — realize after doing.
questions.explanation: Use -고 보니: realize after doing.

questions.prompt:
비가 오네요. 우산을 ___ 그랬어요. (가져오다)
Target grammar: -(으)ㄹ 걸 (그랬다) — regret not doing something.
questions.explanation: The speaker regrets not bringing an umbrella.

questions.prompt:
길이 막혀요. 지하철을 ___ 그랬어요. (타다)
Target grammar: -(으)ㄹ 걸 (그랬다) — regret not doing something.
questions.explanation: Use -(으)ㄹ 걸 (그랬다): regret not doing something.

questions.prompt:
많이 잤___ 아직 졸려요.
Target grammar: -는데도 / -(으)ㄴ데도 / 인데도 — even though.
questions.explanation: Still sleepy despite sleeping a lot.

questions.prompt:
이 가방은 ___ 인기가 많아요. (비싸다: even though)
Target grammar: -는데도 / -(으)ㄴ데도 / 인데도 — even though.
questions.explanation: Use -는데도 / -(으)ㄴ데도 / 인데도: even though.

questions.prompt:
한국 역사___ 발표할 거예요.
Target grammar: 에 대해(서) / 에 대한 — about;regarding.
questions.explanation: 에 대해 marks the topic of the presentation.

questions.prompt:
환경___ 책을 읽었어요. (before a noun)
Target grammar: 에 대해(서) / 에 대한 — about;regarding.
questions.explanation: Use 에 대해(서) / 에 대한: about;regarding.

questions.prompt:

grammar.meaning: remind someone of a known fact

questions.prompt:

questions.prompt:
한국어는 배우면 배울___ 재미있어요.
Target grammar: -(으)면 -(으)ㄹ수록 — the more…the more.

questions.prompt:

questions.prompt:

questions.explanation: Use -는 척하다 / -(으)ㄴ 척하다 / 인 척하다: pretend to be or do.

questions.prompt:

questions.explanation: Use -았/었던 / 이었던: past recollection or former state.

questions.prompt:
지금은 가게가 문을 닫았___ .

민수 씨는 지금 집에 있___.

questions.explanation: Use -(으)ㄹ걸요 / 일걸요: tentative assumption.

questions.prompt:

questions.prompt:

questions.prompt:

questions.prompt:

questions.prompt:

questions.prompt:

questions.prompt:

Target grammar: -는 모양이다 / -(으)ㄴ 모양이다 / 인 모양이다 — it seems based on evidence.
questions.explanation: Use -는 모양이다 / -(으)ㄴ 모양이다 / 인 모양이다: it seems based on evidence.

grammar.meaning: hope or worry that something needs to happen

questions.prompt:
내일 면접을 잘 봐야 ___ 걱정이에요.
Target grammar: -아/어야 할 텐데 / 이어야 할 텐데 — hope or worry that something needs to happen.
questions.explanation: Expresses concern about an outcome that needs to go well.

questions.prompt:
버스가 빨리 와야 ___ 늦겠어요.
Target grammar: -아/어야 할 텐데 / 이어야 할 텐데 — hope or worry that something needs to happen.
questions.explanation: Use -아/어야 할 텐데 / 이어야 할 텐데: hope or worry that something needs to happen.

questions.prompt:

Target grammar: -는다면 / -다면 / (이)라면 — if (hypothetical).
questions.explanation: Use -는다면 / -다면 / (이)라면: if (hypothetical).

questions.prompt:

questions.explanation: 언제든지 refers to any time.

questions.prompt:

questions.explanation: Use 누구든(지), 언제든(지), 어디든(지), 무엇이든(지): anyone;anytime;anywhere;anything.

questions.prompt:

questions.prompt:

questions.explanation: Use -는다니까(요) / -다니까(요) / (이)라니까(요): insist or repeat emphatically.
